# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for a single-node test of the AMG2023 benchmark
# on an AWS ARM-based CPU instance within a Kubernetes environment using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a unique name to prevent collisions with previous experiments.
  name: amg-test-1
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 for the initial node test.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. For a single-node test,
  # this often matches the number of cores, but for a simple functional test, 1 is sufficient.
  tasks: 1

  # The main application container that will run the benchmark.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute within the container. Flux will prepend the necessary MPI launch command.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a small problem size (4x4x4 grid).
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4
      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the MiniCluster pods.
      launcher: false
      # Requesting an AWS EFA device for high-performance networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture is ARM, as required for AWS Graviton instances.
    arch: arm
    # Specify the ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that any errors or unexpected outputs are treated as failures.
    strict: true

  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods and services upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves the task-to-processor mismatch
# and incorporates performance optimizations for running the AMG benchmark on AWS ARM instances.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Using a new name to avoid collisions with the failed attempt.
  name: amg-test-2
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, kept at 1 for the single-node test.
  size: 1
  # Corrected the number of tasks to 64 to match the processor topology (4x4x4=64)
  # required by the application command '-P 4 4 4'.
  tasks: 64

  # The job will not be retried on failure, allowing for direct inspection of logs.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Pods will not be restarted so logs can be inspected on failure.
  pod:
    restartPolicy: Never

  # The main application container that runs the benchmark.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to execute. Flux will prepend the necessary MPI launch command.
      # Runs AMG with problem type 2 and a 4x4x4 processor grid.
      command: amg -problem 2 -P 4 4 4
      # This container is a worker, not the one that launches the MiniCluster pods.
      launcher: false
      # Environment variables for performance tuning and enabling EFA networking.
      environment:
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
        OMPI_MCA_pml: cm
        OMPI_MCA_mtl: ofi
        OMPI_MCA_mtl_ofi_provider_include: efa
        FI_PROVIDER: efa
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
      # Requesting an AWS EFA device for high-performance networking.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and workers.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture is ARM for AWS Graviton instances.
    arch: arm
    # Specify the ARM-compatible Flux container image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
    # Add Flux option flag to ensure each task is bound to a specific CPU for performance.
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that any errors or unexpected outputs are treated as failures.
    strict: true

  # Do not automatically delete the MiniCluster pods and services upon completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs.
  cleanup: false
